summary: The paper rigorously optimizes and tightens the finite-dimensional algebraic primitives in both stages of the Liu-Zhang-Ren (LZR) deterministic subexponential DLP framework. All three main theorems—exact non-calculus potential optimization yielding 64x-227x Stage-I threshold compression, unconditional minimal filter degree 4w-2 under integer-only nonnegativity, and composite-modulus HNF coset halving with Fischer-Hadamard M-matrix determinant and F_r-nullity bounds—are mathematically sound, numerically verified, and cleanly scoped across Lean 4.36.0 and zero-float rational certificates.
strengths: Theorem 1(a)-(b) derives the exact global optimizer lambda* = c0/(sqrt(c1)(1-sqrt(c1))) and delta_max = (1-sqrt(c1))^2/c0 via two elementary perfect-square identities (with automatic W_S > 0 when lambda > a), achieving 64x-227x Stage-I threshold compression.

Theorem 2 proves strict unreachability of LZR's extreme roots j=+-w for w >= 2 and establishes 4w-2 as the unconditional minimal degree even among real polynomials constrained only to integer nonnegativity on I_{w,M_lab}.

Theorem 3 gives a clean group-homomorphism proof of composite-modulus HNF coset halving (|A'| <= |A|/2), tightens the Neumann M-matrix determinant bound via Koteljanskii's inequality, and validates end-to-end deterministic DLP/ECDLP recovery on F_23*, F_47*, E(F_17), and E(F_23).
Exceptional verification transparency: 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems with zero axioms/sorry, an AST-audited zero-float Fraction verifier, and explicit scoping.
weaknesses: All improvements are finite-dimensional or constant-factor refinements rather than asymptotic improvements to the 2^{O(b/sqrt(log log b))} complexity, and the full DLP pipeline remains conditional on LZR's Cauchy-Hermite contraction primitive.

In Theorem 1(b), the paper jumps directly to integer lambda=9 without explicitly noting the nearby continuous optima lambda* approx 8.92 at (4,64) and 8.82 at (4,32), and Theorem 3(c) cites LZR's Eq. (4.1) without restating it inline.

General-N Koteljanskii-Fischer M-matrix inequality and the Intermediate Value Theorem step of Theorem 2(b) are proved analytically and checked on finite instances in Python rather than formalized in Lean 4.36.0.
